sources.citation: SEAlang SALA (Southeast Asian Linguistics Archives) full-text search (search.pl) for 'Kayong', 'Kơyong', 'Ca Dong', 'Cagiuong', plus the SALA and MKS-archive language indexes
sources.note: No paper about Kayong exists in either archive (no Kayong entry in the language indexes). Full-text hits for 'Kayong' are only classification tables (Thomas 1966 'Mon-Khmer subgroupings in Vietnam', Thomas 1973 'A note on the branches of Mon-Khmer' MKS 4:139-141), Cooper & Cooper 1966, and false hits (Tagalog kayong, Kuy kasaw).

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog, 'Resources in and about the Kayong language' [kxy] (Internet Archive copy, up-to-date as of 2025-01-23)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No language description listed other than the Glottolog stub; other resources are Ethnologue, LINGUIST List, and an MPI EVA / TLA item 'Word_list_Kayong' (Jakarta Field Station, oai:www.mpi.nl:lat_1839_00_0000_0000_0022_6A7B_6) whose Jakarta provenance suggests it is really the Malayic 'Kayong' of West Kalimantan, not this language (TLA record blocked to anonymous users, so unverified).

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 22nd ed., entry Kayong [kxy] (the Internet Archive capture 2019-09-18; live 2025 page could not be reached by automated download)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Population 25,000 (Bradley 2007b); Kon Tum province, remote mountains, also Quang Ngai; 6a* Vigorous; 'Dialects: None known. Reportedly similar to Takua [tkz] and Cua [cua]'; part of the Xo Dang official ethnic community.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2009. How many branches in a tree? Cua and East (North) Bahnaric. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross, 193-208. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 605.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Kayong phonology or stress. Kayong appears only in the Thomas & Headley 1970 classification table ('7. Kayong (Cagiương)' under North Bahnaric), in the list of North Bahnaric languages, and in fn. 7: Diffloth & Zide 1992 proposed an Eastern 'Cua-Kayong' division; Sidwell's view is that Kayong groups with Jeh-Halăng, 'consistent with the statement of Cooper and Cooper (1966:87) that Kayong is "mutually intelligible with Halăng"'. One Kayong form cited (ɲiem 'year').

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2002. Genetic classification of the Bahnaric languages: a comprehensive review. Mon-Khmer Studies 32: 1-24.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Kayong is not mentioned anywhere in the scanned text (North Bahnaric listed as Bahnar, Jeh, Halang, Monom, Rengao, Sedang, Hre..).

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1973. Eastern North Bahnaric: Cua and Kơtua. Mon-Khmer Studies 4: 113-118.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Kayong or stress; classification of Cua and Kơtua only.

sources.citation: Cooper, James & Nancy Cooper. 1966. Halăng phonemes. Mon-Khmer Studies 2: 87-98.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: This is a description of HALANG (hala1252), not Kayong. p. 87: 'Kơyong, a nearby dialect, is mutually intelligible with Halăng. The speakers of Kơyong live west of Daktô in Kontum Province.' The stress statement (p. 93, sec. 2 Consonant Patterns and Positions) is for Halang: a word has one 'main syllable' which 'receives the heavier stress' and an optional preceding 'preliminary syllable' which 'receives the lighter stress' with a usually mid-central vowel. No Kayong data.

sources.citation: Thomas, David D. 1966. Mon-Khmer subgroupings in Vietnam. In Norman H. Zide (ed.), Studies in Comparative Austroasiatic Linguistics, 194-202. The Hague: Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SALA full-text hit for Kayong (classification table noting Kayong); wordlist-level classification only; useful for identity ('Kayong' vs 'Duan') rather than stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Kayong (kayo1245); plus local Glottolog 5.1 sources.bib and hh.bib entries tagged kxy
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog's most extensive description (Glottolog's most extensive description) for Kayong is Thomas & Headley 1970 at 'a wordlist or less' level; the only refs tagged kxy in the 5.1 bibliography are Thomas & Headley 1970 (Lingua 25), Maitre 1912 (Les Jungles Moï) and Parker 1991 (guide to Austroasiatic speakers), all overviews. Subclassification comment cites Edmondson, Gregerson & Sidwell 2011.

sources.note: No phonology at all; only location (Sa Thầy / Kon Plông, Kon Tum; Ngọc Linh foothills, Quảng Nam / Quảng Ngãi), population c. 25-27,000, classification, and the citations Sidwell 2009 and Sidwell/Edmondson/Gregerson 2011 'The North Bahnaric clade: a computational approach' (Austroasiatic Studies, ICAAL4, pp. 23-37).

sources.note: Comparative/classification paper; the source Glottolog cites for Kayong's subclassification; built on wordlists for every North Bahnaric language including Kayong (probably Gregerson/Edmondson's 2000s Kon Tum field lists), so it is the most likely place for any published Kayong data and a possible phonological note. Not found on SEAlang SALA/MKS archive, ANU ORR or via APIs.
